# LaunchSense

LaunchSense checks the codebase, not the business. The job runs in the coding tool, on the files already on the machine. The website is the first look: a public paste, a plain report, and pages for awareness and case studies.

This stage is alpha. Alpha has no login. An auth slot exists and is not enforced.

## Install

From this repository, run:

```
sh install.sh
```

The script installs the MCP server command and one skill, `launchsense`. That skill governs the review.

## Review

The tool is `launchsense_scan_repo`. It reads the working tree. It does not call api.github.com. It does not upload file bodies.

Guest limits of 200 files and about 2MB apply to the website paste. The local review has its own cap and lists what it did not read. A partial result is not a pass.

## Checks

Fixed checks cover secrets, code shapes, dependency names, license text, and project hygiene. The local review also reads an npm lockfile, asks OSV about up to 50 of those exact versions, and lists how many were not queried. It may ask deps.dev and ClearlyDefined for terms, a publish date, and a deprecated flag. Archived status stays unknown. It can flag repeated function text, duplicate files, a named host, a model card, and a generated marker.

License lines are signals, not legal advice. Unknown stays unknown. A model may quote one next look. That quote is not a finding. The priority table always orders the report. The decision API may reorder inside one severity band. The model does not choose which findings exist.

## Diagnostics

After agreement, alpha and pro may send rule id counts, the harness name, the version, how long the review took, and which order source ran. Enterprise leaves this off. The share does not include code, paths, titles, or function names.

## Do not claim

The review does not say the app will sell. It does not edit the repo. It does not certify anything. It does not treat a source-available license as open source.
